{"parentUuid":"2f0ba73a-37ef-4ec1-9dfc-ac6cb90267ae","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"506b77ab-09a6-4413-8128-0707009ec9af","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PJE5bxnmmV2HUz9MdtgAPH","type":"tool_result","content":"title:\tT01 — Coach and editors log in and out\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tRafaelFrias1\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, ticket\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\tRafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms#4, RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms#3\nnumber:\t2\n--\n## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Coach, Captain and Team manager can log in to the admin console on the team laptop with their email and password, and log out. Nobody can use any console screen without logging in. A deactivated account is refused at login even with the right password. The demo seed creates one admin account and one editor account so the console can be used straight away.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Accounts have an email (unique), an argon2 password hash, a role (`admin` | `editor`) and an active flag; no plain password is ever stored or logged\n- [ ] A correct email and password logs in; a wrong password or unknown email gives the same generic error\n- [ ] A deactivated account is refused at login with the correct password\n- [ ] Logout ends the session\n- [ ] Every console URL except the login page redirects someone who isn't logged in to the login page\n- [ ] The login and logout forms carry a CSRF token; a request without a valid token is rejected\n- [ ] The demo seed creates one admin and one editor, reading their passwords from the environment, and runs clean on a fresh clone\n- [ ] The T00 admin test logs in first (via `client_as(\"admin\")`) and still checks that the console answers with \"hello admin\"; the other T00 tests are unchanged and pass\n- [ ] Tests go through HTTP with the existing `client` / `client_as` fixtures\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone (can start immediately)\ntitle:\tSpec: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tRafaelFrias1\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon men's golf team runs on the team group chat and the coach's emails. Important details are buried within a day, so players ask the same questions every week: when is practice, where is qualifying, am I traveling. Parents can't easily find where the next tournament is or how to follow live scoring. Recruits email the coach for basic information and results. The official athletics site has results, but someone outside the team updates it, sometimes days late, and it says nothing about practice or travel.\n\nThe coach, captain and team manager are not technical. The coach doesn't want to learn new software mid-season. Some content has to be protected: only the coach may change the travel lineup and qualifying results, only the coach may edit the recruiting page (NCAA rules), and editors must never delete past results.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS for the team. Content is written on **the team laptop** in a local admin console, and a static public site, built for phones first, is updated on GitHub Pages.\n\n- The **Coach** (admin) owns every **page** (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and every **qualifying result**, and manages **accounts**.\n- The **Captain** and **Team manager** (editors) write **posts**: the weekly **practice schedule** and **tournament recaps**. They can change only their own posts.\n- Publishing is one click. Any change to published content triggers a **site update**: the public site is rebuilt and deployed automatically (ADR-004). If the deploy fails, the change is not saved, so the console and the website always agree.\n- A **reader** opens the home page on their phone and sees the Travel Lineup, then the newest posts (including this week's practice schedule). The nav links to every page.\n\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n1. As the Coach, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can reach the coach-only parts of the console.\n2. As the Captain, I want to log in with my own account, so that my posts carry my name.\n3. As any account holder, I want to log out, so that the next person on the team laptop can't post as me.\n4. As the Coach, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n5. As any account holder, I want a wrong password to give a generic error, so that nobody can tell which emails have accounts.\n6. As a reader or someone who isn't logged in, I want every console URL to send me to the login page, so that the console is never usable without an account.\n7. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Captain with the editor role, so that they can post the practice schedule.\n8. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Team manager with the editor role, so that they can write recaps.\n9. As the Coach, I want to change an account's role, so that I can correct a role given by mistake.\n10. As the Coach, I want to deactivate a graduated Captain's account, so that they can no longer log in.\n11. As a deactivated Captain, I am refused at login even with the right password, so that former team members can't post.\n12. As the Coach, I want a deactivated account's published posts to stay on the site under its name, so that last season's record isn't lost.\n13. As an admin, I am prevented from deactivating my own account, so that the site always keeps an admin.\n14. As the Webmaster, I want a backup admin account, so that I can recover the site if the Coach is locked out.\n15. As an editor, I am refused the account-management screens, including by typing the URL directly, so that only admins manage accounts (field notes: WordPress hid Users *and* denied the direct link).\n\n### Posts\n16. As the Captain, I want to write a practice schedule post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can format times and places as a list.\n17. As the Captain, I want to save a post as a draft, so that I can finish it later without anyone seeing it.\n18. As the Captain, I want to publish my post with one click, next to Save draft, so that publishing isn't a two-step chore (field notes).\n19. As the Captain, I want the slug generated from the title and made unique automatically (practice-schedule, practice-schedule-2, …), so that I never have to type or think about a slug.\n20. As an admin, I want to edit a slug if needed, so that an important post can have a clean URL.\n21. As the Team manager, I want to write a tournament recap (text only), so that alumni and parents know how the team did.\n22. As the Coach, I want to post qualifying results, so that players and recruits can see them.\n23. As an editor, I want to edit and delete only my own posts, so that the Captain can't change the Coach's results and the Team manager can't change the practice schedule.\n24. As an editor, I am refused when I try to edit or delete someone else's post, even through a direct request, so that the rule holds when the button is hidden.\n25. As the Coach, I want to edit or delete any post, so that I can correct mistakes or remove a botched result.\n26. As any author, I want each post to show its author and its created and updated times, so that readers know how current it is.\n27. As an editor, I want to unpublish my own post, so that I can take down something posted by mistake.\n\n### Pages\n28. As the Coach, I want to create and edit the Season Schedule page, including live-scoring links, so that parents know where the next tournament is and how to follow it.\n29. As the Coach, I want to update the Travel Lineup page in place once, so that I stop texting it to eight people.\n30. As the Coach, I want to edit the Recruiting page with my contact details, so that recruits can reach me without emailing for basics, and so that its content stays NCAA-compliant.\n31. As an editor, I am refused all page creation, editing and deletion, so that every coach-only page is protected by one simple rule.\n32. As a reader, I want every published page in the site navigation, so that I can find the schedule, lineup and recruiting info from any page.\n33. As the Coach, I want draft pages to stay out of the navigation, so that a half-written page never shows up.\n\n### Admin console\n34. As the Coach, I want a dashboard with counts of posts and pages by status, so that I can see what's in draft at a glance.\n35. As any account holder, I want posts and pages in one content list, so that I don't have to hunt for separate menus (field notes).\n36. As any account holder, I want one filter bar on that list (status first, then type and author), so that the status filter isn't hidden away (field notes).\n37. As any account holder, I want to preview the rendered Markdown before publishing, so that I can check formatting.\n38. As an editor, I want the console to show only the actions I'm allowed (no page or account controls), so that I'm not confused by buttons that would fail.\n\n### Publishing and the public site\n39. As the Captain, I want my published post to be on the website without any extra step, so that players see the schedule right away.\n40. As the Coach, I want the site to update automatically whenever I publish, edit, unpublish or delete published content, so that I never have to remember a second button.\n41. As the Coach, editing the Travel Lineup without wifi, I want an error and my typed text kept in the form, with the live lineup left unchanged, so that I can retry with wifi without retyping anything.\n42. As an editor, if a site update fails when I publish, I want my post to stay a draft and be told to try again later, so that \"Published\" in the console always means \"on the website\".\n43. As a player, I want the home page to show the Travel Lineup first and then the newest posts, so that one page on my phone answers \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\".\n44. As a parent, I want the Season Schedule in the navigation, so that I can find the next tournament and its live-scoring link.\n45. As a recruit, I want to find results and the coach's contact without emailing, so that I can evaluate the program on my own.\n46. As an alumnus, I want recaps and results listed newest first, so that I can follow how the team is doing.\n47. As a reader, I want the public site readable on a phone with no horizontal scrolling, so that I can check it at the course.\n48. As a reader, I never see draft content, so that unfinished posts stay private.\n49. As a reader, I'm protected from script injection in any post or page, so that a pasted snippet can't run code in my browser.\n50. As the Webmaster, I want every link and asset in the public site to use a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles.** Exactly two: admin and editor. The Coach and the Webmaster are admins; the Captain and Team manager are editors. Accounts are per person and are never deleted, only deactivated.\n- **Permission rules**, enforced on the server for every request, not only by hiding buttons:\n  - Admin: everything.\n  - Editor: create posts; edit, publish, unpublish and delete only posts they authored; no pages; no account management.\n  - Nobody may deactivate their own account.\n  - Qualifying results have no special type. They are protected because the Coach authors them and editors can't touch others' posts.\n- **Content model.** One content item shape, with a kind of `post` or `page`, a title, a unique slug (generated from the title and de-duplicated; admins may edit it), a Markdown body, a status (`draft` | `published`), an author account, and created and updated timestamps. Posts and pages share one table/model and one editor; \"kind\" drives navigation and permissions.\n- **Account model.** Email (unique), argon2 password hash, role, active flag. Login fails for inactive accounts.\n- **Sessions.** Signed session cookies. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token, and requests without a valid token are rejected.\n- **Markdown.** Rendered with the Markdown library, then sanitized with the HTML sanitizer before it goes anywhere: preview, console, or `site/`. Images are not part of the allowed output.\n- **Site update module.** One operation, \"update the site\": render all published content into `site/`, then deploy it to `gh-pages`. The console runs it after any change to published content: publish, edit of a published item, unpublish, and delete of a published item. Account changes (including deactivation) never trigger one.\n  - The change and the site update form one unit. The change is staged, the site is rebuilt from the would-be state, and the deploy is attempted. Only after a successful deploy is the change committed; on failure it is rolled back and the form is re-shown with the user's input and an error.\n  - Draft-only changes (saving or deleting a draft) never trigger a site update.\n  - The deployer is injected through `create_app()` (default: push `site/` to `gh-pages` via ghp-import; the GitHub token comes from the environment). See ADR-004.\n- **Public site rendering.** Builds on the existing `render_site(out)`. It writes a home page (the Travel Lineup page content if published, then published posts newest first), one HTML file per published post and page, and a navigation built from published pages. Every `href`/`src` is relative. Styling is mobile-first.\n- **Travel Lineup on the home page.** Identified by its slug (`travel-lineup`), not by a new field.\n- **Console.** Login/logout; a dashboard with counts by kind and status; one content list with a single filter bar (status, kind, author); an editor with Save draft and Publish side by side and a Markdown preview; account management (admin only): create, change role, deactivate/reactivate.\n- **CLI.** `cms publish` and `cms deploy` remain for the Webmaster. They call the same site update module.\n- **ADRs respected.** ADR-001 (local console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack, no new dependencies), ADR-004 (publish auto-deploys, failure blocks the change).\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **Good tests check external behaviour only:** HTTP status codes, redirects, what a page shows, and the files written to `site/`. They never inspect internal functions or database rows when a response or an output file can show the same thing.\n- **Seam 1: HTTP.** The existing `TestClient` + `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` (prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`). Covers login and logout, deactivated login refusal, CSRF rejection, the editor vs admin permission matrix (including direct requests to forbidden URLs, per the field notes), post/page CRUD, slug de-duplication, dashboard counts, filters, and preview sanitizing.\n- **Seam 2: rendering.** `render_site(out)` into a temporary directory. Covers: drafts never written; Markdown sanitized (`<script>` stripped); nav built from published pages only; the home page shows the Travel Lineup then newest posts; and no root-absolute `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` anywhere.\n- **Seam 3: deployer (new).** `create_app()` accepts a deployer; tests pass a fake that records calls or raises. Covers: publishing calls the deployer once; a draft save never calls it; when the deployer fails, the item keeps its previous state (still draft, or the old published text) and the response re-shows the user's input with an error. No test ever touches the network or GitHub.\n- The demo users seeded for tests are one admin and one editor; permission tests that need a second editor (to prove \"own posts only\") create one through the admin's account-management route.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Photos, media upload and images in posts (recaps are text only).\n- Posting from a phone; the console runs only on the team laptop and is never on the public internet.\n- Search, comments, contact forms, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Scheduled (future-dated) publishing and revision history/undo.\n- A separate \"qualifying result\" post type, categories or tags.\n- Password reset by email; self-service sign-up.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, WYSIWYG editors.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Trust risk accepted:** the Captain is a player and could post scores in a practice-schedule post; the CMS relies on trust there rather than a result type.\n- **Operational risk accepted (ADR-004):** the team laptop holds a GitHub push token (from the environment, never committed) and must be online to publish.\n- The client brief's delete rule was revised during grilling: \"Only the coach can delete past results. Editors can never delete them.\"\n- Field-note findings that became requirements: one-click Publish, one filter bar with status first, posts and pages in one list, and access control that denies direct URLs as well as hiding menu items.\n\n\"\"\"IPHS 400 MP2 — your CMS package.\n\nT00 ships a skeleton only: one admin page, one public page, and a publish step.\nEverything else (login, roles, posts, pages, users) is yours to build, one\nticket at a time.\n\"\"\"\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — The demo seed creates one admin account and one editor account so the console can be used straight away.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Accounts have an email (unique), an argon2 password hash, a role (`admin` | `editor`) and an active flag; no plain password is ever stored or logged\n- [ ] A correct email and password logs in; a wrong password or unknown email gives the same generic error\n- [ ] A deactivated account is refused at login with the correct password\n- [ ] Logout ends the session\n- [ ] Every console URL except the login page redirects someone who isn't logged in to the login page\n- [ ] The login and logout forms carry a CSRF token; a request without a valid token is rejected\n- [ ] The demo seed creates one admin and one editor, reading their passwords from the environment, and runs clean on a fresh clone\n- [ ] The T00 admin test logs in first (via `client_as(\"admin\")`) and still checks that the console answers with \"hello admin\"; the other T00 tests are unchanged and pass\n- [ ] Tests go through HTTP with the existing `client` / `client_as` fixtures\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone (can start immediately)\ntitle:\tSpec: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tRafaelFrias1\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon men's golf team runs on the team group chat and the coach's emails. Important details are buried within a day, so players ask the same questions every week: when is practice, where is qualifying, am I traveling. Parents can't easily find where the next tournament is or how to follow live scoring. Recruits email the coach for basic information and results. The official athletics site has results, but someone outside the team updates it, sometimes days late, and it says nothing about practice or travel.\n\nThe coach, captain and team manager are not technical. The coach doesn't want to learn new software mid-season. Some content has to be protected: only the coach may change the travel lineup and qualifying results, only the coach may edit the recruiting page (NCAA rules), and editors must never delete past results.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS for the team. Content is written on **the team laptop** in a local admin console, and a static public site, built for phones first, is updated on GitHub Pages.\n\n- The **Coach** (admin) owns every **page** (Season Schedule, Travel Lineup, Recruiting) and every **qualifying result**, and manages **accounts**.\n- The **Captain** and **Team manager** (editors) write **posts**: the weekly **practice schedule** and **tournament recaps**. They can change only their own posts.\n- Publishing is one click. Any change to published content triggers a **site update**: the public site is rebuilt and deployed automatically (ADR-004). If the deploy fails, the change is not saved, so the console and the website always agree.\n- A **reader** opens the home page on their phone and sees the Travel Lineup, then the newest posts (including this week's practice schedule). The nav links to every page.\n\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n1. As the Coach, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can reach the coach-only parts of the console.\n2. As the Captain, I want to log in with my own account, so that my posts carry my name.\n3. As any account holder, I want to log out, so that the next person on the team laptop can't post as me.\n4. As the Coach, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n5. As any account holder, I want a wrong password to give a generic error, so that nobody can tell which emails have accounts.\n6. As a reader or someone who isn't logged in, I want every console URL to send me to the login page, so that the console is never usable without an account.\n7. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Captain with the editor role, so that they can post the practice schedule.\n8. As the Coach, I want to create an account for this season's Team manager with the editor role, so that they can write recaps.\n9. As the Coach, I want to change an account's role, so that I can correct a role given by mistake.\n10. As the Coach, I want to deactivate a graduated Captain's account, so that they can no longer log in.\n11. As a deactivated Captain, I am refused at login even with the right password, so that former team members can't post.\n12. As the Coach, I want a deactivated account's published posts to stay on the site under its name, so that last season's record isn't lost.\n13. As an admin, I am prevented from deactivating my own account, so that the site always keeps an admin.\n14. As the Webmaster, I want a backup admin account, so that I can recover the site if the Coach is locked out.\n15. As an editor, I am refused the account-management screens, including by typing the URL directly, so that only admins manage accounts (field notes: WordPress hid Users *and* denied the direct link).\n\n### Posts\n16. As the Captain, I want to write a practice schedule post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can format times and places as a list.\n17. As the Captain, I want to save a post as a draft, so that I can finish it later without anyone seeing it.\n18. As the Captain, I want to publish my post with one click, next to Save draft, so that publishing isn't a two-step chore (field notes).\n19. As the Captain, I want the slug generated from the title and made unique automatically (practice-schedule, practice-schedule-2, …), so that I never have to type or think about a slug.\n20. As an admin, I want to edit a slug if needed, so that an important post can have a clean URL.\n21. As the Team manager, I want to write a tournament recap (text only), so that alumni and parents know how the team did.\n22. As the Coach, I want to post qualifying results, so that players and recruits can see them.\n23. As an editor, I want to edit and delete only my own posts, so that the Captain can't change the Coach's results and the Team manager can't change the practice schedule.\n24. As an editor, I am refused when I try to edit or delete someone else's post, even through a direct request, so that the rule holds when the button is hidden.\n25. As the Coach, I want to edit or delete any post, so that I can correct mistakes or remove a botched result.\n26. As any author, I want each post to show its author and its created and updated times, so that readers know how current it is.\n27. As an editor, I want to unpublish my own post, so that I can take down something posted by mistake.\n\n### Pages\n28. As the Coach, I want to create and edit the Season Schedule page, including live-scoring links, so that parents know where the next tournament is and how to follow it.\n29. As the Coach, I want to update the Travel Lineup page in place once, so that I stop texting it to eight people.\n30. As the Coach, I want to edit the Recruiting page with my contact details, so that recruits can reach me without emailing for basics, and so that its content stays NCAA-compliant.\n31. As an editor, I am refused all page creation, editing and deletion, so that every coach-only page is protected by one simple rule.\n32. As a reader, I want every published page in the site navigation, so that I can find the schedule, lineup and recruiting info from any page.\n33. As the Coach, I want draft pages to stay out of the navigation, so that a half-written page never shows up.\n\n### Admin console\n34. As the Coach, I want a dashboard with counts of posts and pages by status, so that I can see what's in draft at a glance.\n35. As any account holder, I want posts and pages in one content list, so that I don't have to hunt for separate menus (field notes).\n36. As any account holder, I want one filter bar on that list (status first, then type and author), so that the status filter isn't hidden away (field notes).\n37. As any account holder, I want to preview the rendered Markdown before publishing, so that I can check formatting.\n38. As an editor, I want the console to show only the actions I'm allowed (no page or account controls), so that I'm not confused by buttons that would fail.\n\n### Publishing and the public site\n39. As the Captain, I want my published post to be on the website without any extra step, so that players see the schedule right away.\n40. As the Coach, I want the site to update automatically whenever I publish, edit, unpublish or delete published content, so that I never have to remember a second button.\n41. As the Coach, editing the Travel Lineup without wifi, I want an error and my typed text kept in the form, with the live lineup left unchanged, so that I can retry with wifi without retyping anything.\n42. As an editor, if a site update fails when I publish, I want my post to stay a draft and be told to try again later, so that \"Published\" in the console always means \"on the website\".\n43. As a player, I want the home page to show the Travel Lineup first and then the newest posts, so that one page on my phone answers \"am I traveling\" and \"when is practice\".\n44. As a parent, I want the Season Schedule in the navigation, so that I can find the next tournament and its live-scoring link.\n45. As a recruit, I want to find results and the coach's contact without emailing, so that I can evaluate the program on my own.\n46. As an alumnus, I want recaps and results listed newest first, so that I can follow how the team is doing.\n47. As a reader, I want the public site readable on a phone with no horizontal scrolling, so that I can check it at the course.\n48. As a reader, I never see draft content, so that unfinished posts stay private.\n49. As a reader, I'm protected from script injection in any post or page, so that a pasted snippet can't run code in my browser.\n50. As the Webmaster, I want every link and asset in the public site to use a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles.** Exactly two: admin and editor. The Coach and the Webmaster are admins; the Captain and Team manager are editors. Accounts are per person and are never deleted, only deactivated.\n- **Permission rules**, enforced on the server for every request, not only by hiding buttons:\n  - Admin: everything.\n  - Editor: create posts; edit, publish, unpublish and delete only posts they authored; no pages; no account management.\n  - Nobody may deactivate their own account.\n  - Qualifying results have no special type. They are protected because the Coach authors them and editors can't touch others' posts.\n- **Content model.** One content item shape, with a kind of `post` or `page`, a title, a unique slug (generated from the title and de-duplicated; admins may edit it), a Markdown body, a status (`draft` | `published`), an author account, and created and updated timestamps. Posts and pages share one table/model and one editor; \"kind\" drives navigation and permissions.\n- **Account model.** Email (unique), argon2 password hash, role, active flag. Login fails for inactive accounts.\n- **Sessions.** Signed session cookies. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token, and requests without a valid token are rejected.\n- **Markdown.** Rendered with the Markdown library, then sanitized with the HTML sanitizer before it goes anywhere: preview, console, or `site/`. Images are not part of the allowed output.\n- **Site update module.** One operation, \"update the site\": render all published content into `site/`, then deploy it to `gh-pages`. The console runs it after any change to published content: publish, edit of a published item, unpublish, and delete of a published item. Account changes (including deactivation) never trigger one.\n  - The change and the site update form one unit. The change is staged, the site is rebuilt from the would-be state, and the deploy is attempted. Only after a successful deploy is the change committed; on failure it is rolled back and the form is re-shown with the user's input and an error.\n  - Draft-only changes (saving or deleting a draft) never trigger a site update.\n  - The deployer is injected through `create_app()` (default: push `site/` to `gh-pages` via ghp-import; the GitHub token comes from the environment). See ADR-004.\n- **Public site rendering.** Builds on the existing `render_site(out)`. It writes a home page (the Travel Lineup page content if published, then published posts newest first), one HTML file per published post and page, and a navigation built from published pages. Every `href`/`src` is relative. Styling is mobile-first.\n- **Travel Lineup on the home page.** Identified by its slug (`travel-lineup`), not by a new field.\n- **Console.** Login/logout; a dashboard with counts by kind and status; one content list with a single filter bar (status, kind, author); an editor with Save draft and Publish side by side and a Markdown preview; account management (admin only): create, change role, deactivate/reactivate.\n- **CLI.** `cms publish` and `cms deploy` remain for the Webmaster. They call the same site update module.\n- **ADRs respected.** ADR-001 (local console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack, no new dependencies), ADR-004 (publish auto-deploys, failure blocks the change).\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **Good tests check external behaviour only:** HTTP status codes, redirects, what a page shows, and the files written to `site/`. They never inspect internal functions or database rows when a response or an output file can show the same thing.\n- **Seam 1: HTTP.** The existing `TestClient` + `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` (prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`). Covers login and logout, deactivated login refusal, CSRF rejection, the editor vs admin permission matrix (including direct requests to forbidden URLs, per the field notes), post/page CRUD, slug de-duplication, dashboard counts, filters, and preview sanitizing.\n- **Seam 2: rendering.** `render_site(out)` into a temporary directory. Covers: drafts never written; Markdown sanitized (`<script>` stripped); nav built from published pages only; the home page shows the Travel Lineup then newest posts; and no root-absolute `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` anywhere.\n- **Seam 3: deployer (new).** `create_app()` accepts a deployer; tests pass a fake that records calls or raises. Covers: publishing calls the deployer once; a draft save never calls it; when the deployer fails, the item keeps its previous state (still draft, or the old published text) and the response re-shows the user's input with an error. No test ever touches the network or GitHub.\n- The demo users seeded for tests are one admin and one editor; permission tests that need a second editor (to prove \"own posts only\") create one through the admin's account-management route.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Photos, media upload and images in posts (recaps are text only).\n- Posting from a phone; the console runs only on the team laptop and is never on the public internet.\n- Search, comments, contact forms, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Scheduled (future-dated) publishing and revision history/undo.\n- A separate \"qualifying result\" post type, categories or tags.\n- Password reset by email; self-service sign-up.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, WYSIWYG editors.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Trust risk accepted:** the Captain is a player and could post scores in a practice-schedule post; the CMS relies on trust there rather than a result type.\n- **Operational risk accepted (ADR-004):** the team laptop holds a GitHub push token (from the environment, never committed) and must be online to publish.\n- The client brief's delete rule was revised during grilling: \"Only the coach can delete past results. Editors can never delete them.\"\n- Field-note findings that became requirements: one-click Publish, one filter bar with status first, posts and pages in one list, and access control that denies direct URLs as well as hiding menu items.\n\n\"\"\"IPHS 400 MP2 — your CMS package.\n\nT00 ships a skeleton only: one admin page, one public page, and a publish step.\nEverything else (login, roles, posts, pages, users) is yours to build, one\nticket at a time.\n\"\"\"\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = \"\")\n[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n\"\"\"T00: the walking skeleton. Now build ticket T01.</p>\n{% endblock %}\n# Copy to .env (which is gitignored) and change the values.\nCMS_SECRET_KEY=change-me-to-a-long-random-string\nCMS_SITE_TITLE=Knox County Historical Society\nCMS_DATABASE=cms.db\n# Demo accounts created by scripts/seed_demo.py\nCMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-admin\nCMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD=change-me-editor\n# Set after you deploy, e.g. https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nCMS_BASE_PATH=\n# Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping anyone.\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\nADR-002-stack.md\nADR-003-stop-hook-reads-transcript.md\nADR-004-publish-auto-deploys.md\n# Agent instructions\n\n<!-- ai-swe-setup:long-sessions v1 — managed block: bin/repo-standardize in ~/code/ai-swe-setup replaces it; edit the source there -->\n## Long sessions (shared standard)\n- Session handoffs are dated, write-once files in `docs/handoffs/`. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n  here than in a JavaScript stack. The posters (coach,\ncaptain, team manager) are not technical and post mid-season; the whole point of\nthe site is that players stop asking \"when is practice?\" in the group chat. A\npractice schedule that is \"published\" but not on the website fails that goal.\n\nOptions considered: an admin-only \"Update public site\" button (editors' posts\nwait for the coach); a button any account can press (posters must remember a\nsecond step); the webmaster running `cms publish` and `cms deploy` by hand\n(readers wait hours); rebuilding and deploying automatically on every change to\npublished content.\n\n## Decision\n\nAny change to published content (publish, edit, unpublish, delete) triggers a\nsite update: rebuild `site/` and deploy it to the `gh-pages` branch. If the\ndeploy fails, the publish fails too. \"old-captain@example.test\", \"right-pw\")\n    assert response.status_code == 401\n    assert GENERIC_ERROR in response.text\n\n\ndef test_deactivating_a_logged_in_account_ends_its_session(client_as, db_path):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    editor = accounts.find_by_email(db_path, DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"email\"])\n    accounts.set_active(db_path, editor.id, False)\n    response = c.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n\n\ndef test_logout_ends_the_session(client_as, csrf):\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    response = c.post(\"/logout\", data={\"csrf_token\": csrf(c, \"/admin\")},\n                      follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n    assert c.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).headers[\"location\"] == response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n\n\ndef test_login_page_is_reachable_without_logging_in(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/login\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert 'name=\"csrf_token\"' in response.text\n\n\ndef test_login_without_a_csrf_token_is_rejected(client):\n    response = client.post(\"/login\", data={\n        \"email\": == 403\n\n\ndef test_logout_without_a_csrf_token_is_rejected(client_as):\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    assert c.post(\"/logout\", follow_redirects=False).status_code == 403\n    assert test_demo_seed_refuses_to_run_without_passwords(tmp_path):\n    db = tmp_path / \"fresh.db\"\n    result = _run_seed(db)\n    assert result.returncode == 1\n    assert not {"parentUuid":"e25c285f-4aa7-4db9-81de-dad6c2de9f4f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg3KiPnoEdzZUA4TAFbif","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012jhvSKehws8LyXhCxGhFMR","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/accounts.py","content":"\"\"\"Accounts: one person's login, with one role (see CONTEXT.md).\n\nPasswords are stored only as argon2 hashes and are never logged. Accounts are\nnever deleted, only deactivated; a deactivated account cannot log in.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom functools import cache\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom argon2 import PasswordHasher\nfrom argon2.exceptions import InvalidHashError, VerificationError\n\nfrom app import db\n\nROLES = (\"admin\", \"editor\")\n\n_hasher = PasswordHasher()\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Account:\n    id: int\n    email: str\n    role: str\n    active: bool\n\n\ndef _account(row) -> Account:\n    return Account(id=row[\"id\"], email=row[\"email\"], role=row[\"role\"],\n                   active=bool(row[\"active\"]))\n\n\ndef _normalize(email: str) -> str:\n    return email.strip().lower()\n\n\ndef create_account(db_path: Path, email: str, password: str, role: str) -> Account:\n    if role not in ROLES:\n        raise ValueError(f\"Unknown role: {role!r}\")\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        cursor = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO accounts (email, password_hash, role) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n            (_normalize(email), _hasher.hash(password), role),\n        )\n    return get_account(db_path, cursor.lastrowid)\n\n\ndef get_account(db_path: Path, account_id: int) -> Account | None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ?\",\n                           (account_id,)).fetchone()\n    return _account(row) if row else None\n\n\ndef find_by_email(db_path: Path, email: str) -> Account | None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE email = ?\",\n                           (_normalize(email),)).fetchone()\n    return _account(row) if row else None\n\n\ndef set_active(db_path: Path, account_id: int, active: bool) -> None:\n    with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"UPDATE accounts SET active = ? scripts/seed_demo.py\nrebuilds it on a fresh clone.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (active IN (0, 1))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect(path: Path) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open the database, commit on success, roll back on error, always close.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n    try:\n        with conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the tables if they do not exist yet.\"\"\"\n    with connect(path) as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"e25c285f-4aa7-4db9-81de-dad6c2de9f4f","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c59aef1b-1730-4793-ae15-69d04d1a3927","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

As you build content types, extend this so it creates:\n  - one admin and one editor (passwords read from .env, never hard-coded)\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    # TODO (your tickets): create the users, then the demo content.\n    print(\"Nothing to seed yet: no content types exist. \"\n          \"Extend scripts/seed_demo.py as you build T01+.\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c28bee71-5dfe-49ba-bb6a-1b8e052c73dd","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c59aef1b-1730-4793-ae15-69d04d1a3927","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"59f045e2-a869-40c1-9625-600f8d32abf3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg3Kjtqp5ebyCMfeEWTap","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CaPA61CvhNK6vzqNSWtNUu","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/web.py","content":"\"\"\"What every console route shares: templates, CSRF, and who is logged in.\n\nTwo dependencies do the guarding:\n\n  - `verify_csrf` goes on every state-changing (POST) route. Routes live in their own modules under app/routes/ and are\nincluded here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import auth, console\nfrom app.web import LoginRequired, templates\n\n\ndef create_app(db_path: Path | None = None) -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.state.db_path = db_path or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    db.init(app.state.db_path)\n\n    # Signed session cookie that ends when the browser closes (shared laptop).\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=None,\n                       same_site=\"lax\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3145,"cache_read_input_tokens":67135,"output_tokens":2549,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":156},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3145,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2549,"cache_read_input_tokens":67135,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3145,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3145},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01HLLt8kDev7jetZ87QpNkA2":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/main.py","content":"\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console lives under /admin and needs a login (/login); the public\nsite answers at /. Put it in every form.\"\"\"\n    if \"csrf\" not in request.session:\n        request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return request.session[\"csrf\"]\n\n\ntemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\n\n\ndef verify_csrf(request: Request, csrf_token: str = Form(\"\")) -> None:\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not (expected and hmac.compare_digest(expected, csrf_token)):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n\n\ndef current_account(request: Request) -> Account:\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = (accounts.get_account(request.app.state.db_path, account_id)\n               if account_id is not None else None)\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        request.session.clear()\n        raise LoginRequired\n    request.state.account = account\n    return account\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"204f4ae5-5d92-4b70-b772-3ae17722fbf9","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c59aef1b-1730-4793-ae15-69d04d1a3927","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"303958f0-dbc0-43dc-b86e-ea25c7e92abd","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"506b77ab-09a6-4413-8128-0707009ec9af","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012YJm6MupmypCaEKqfBdGof","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/auth.py (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"9988645b-f93a-446b-9763-324107f91da0","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:37:08.030Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/auth.py","content":"\"\"\"Logging in and out of the admin console.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import accounts\nfrom app.web import templates, verify_csrf\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\n# The same message for a wrong password, an unknown email and a deactivated\n# account, so the response never reveals which emails have accounts.\nLOGIN_ERROR = \"Incorrect email or password.\"\n\n\n@router.get(\"/login\")\ndef login_form(request: Request):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/login.html\",\n                                      {\"title\": \"Log in\", \"email\": \"\"})\n\n\n@router.post(\"/login\", dependencies=[Depends(verify_csrf)])\ndef login(request: Request, email: str = Form(\"\"), password: str = Form(\"\")):\n    account = accounts.authenticate(request.app.state.db_path, email, password)\n    if account is None:\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/login.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"Log in\", \"email\": email, \"error\": LOGIN_ERROR},\n            status_code=401,\n        )\n    # A fresh session on login, so a session id or CSRF token planted before\n    # login is worthless afterwards.\n    request.session.clear()\n    request.session[\"account_id\"] = account.id\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/logout\", dependencies=[Depends(verify_csrf)])\ndef logout(request: Request):\n    request.session.clear()\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"303958f0-dbc0-43dc-b86e-ea25c7e92abd","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c59aef1b-1730-4793-ae15-69d04d1a3927","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

Every route on this router requires a logged-in account.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request\n\nfrom app.accounts import Account\nfrom app.web import current_account, templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin\", dependencies=[Depends(current_account)])\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef admin_home(request: Request, account: Account = Depends(current_account)):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"account\": account}\n    )\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"5cb384d0-319a-445e-8caf-82694c28e216","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"4d76fb33-67f7-426c-a6b4-e10410ba73b3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"c59aef1b-1730-4793-ae15-69d04d1a3927","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

Routes live in their own modules under app/routes/ and are\nincluded here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import auth, console\nfrom app.web import LoginRequired, templates\n\n\ndef create_app(db_path: Path | None = None) -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.state.db_path = db_path or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    db.init(app.state.db_path)\n\n    # Signed session cookie that ends when the browser closes (shared laptop).\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=None,\n                       same_site=\"lax\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":31,"newStart":1,"newLines":36,"lines":[" \"\"\"The FastAPI application."," ","-T00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site","-answers at /. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"c59aef1b-1730-4793-ae15-69d04d1a3927","hash":"631b40bdf176f2209d463547313eadebf87f8635860f8c02ee9a60cdb72ef20e","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_01A9RgL7aFMjnZumbhuRyudM","content":"Launching skill: mattpocock-skills:code-review"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/refiv/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). {"parentUuid":"f9ed573a-9e67-4070-aed9-b0cdc7084374","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"506b77ab-09a6-4413-8128-0707009ec9af","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/refiv/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: since HEAD (uncommitted T01 work: app/, scripts/seed_demo.py, templates/admin/, tests/). Spec: issue #2 (T01), parent spec issue #1.
